theysay.say: So-called Black man — you're not African, you're an Israelite. Wake up.
theysay.quick: Receive the compliment inside it: they're saying you matter to God's story. You do — but Scripture locates your place in that story by faith in the Messiah, not by decoding your skin (Gal 3:26-29). Ask: 'Show me the verse that identifies me by my appearance.'

theysay.say: Deuteronomy 28:68 — slave ships! The Most High said you'd go back into bondage in ships. Prove me wrong.
theysay.quick: Read the whole chapter, not the one verse. Verse 68's ships sail to Egypt ('again'), and it ends 'no man shall buy you' — the Atlantic trade's horror was that millions WERE bought. Josephus records Rome literally shipping Jewish captives to Egypt after AD 70.

theysay.say: The people over in Israel today are Khazars — converts, impostors sitting in your seat.
theysay.quick: A 2013 genome-wide study by more than twenty geneticists found no evidence of Khazar origin — Ashkenazi Jews cluster with Middle Eastern populations and other Jewish communities. And Paul still calls unbelieving Israel 'beloved for the sake of the fathers' (Rom 11:28).

theysay.say: Christianity is the slave master's religion. They gave you that white Jesus to keep you docile.
theysay.quick: The wound here is real — slaveholder religion existed and it was wicked. But Ethiopia and Egypt had thriving churches 1,400 years before the first slave ship. Slaveholders printed a 'Slave Bible' with Exodus cut out — because the real Bible sets people free.

theysay.say: Revelation 1 — hair like wool, feet like burnt brass. Jesus was a Black man like you.
theysay.quick: Keep reading the verse: hair 'white like wool, white as snow,' feet like bronze 'glowing in a furnace,' face 'like the sun.' It's a vision of blazing glory echoing Daniel 7 — John fell down as though dead. Jesus was a brown-skinned Judean, and no one at the throne is checking complexions.

theysay.say: The Bible is a book about Black people, by Black people. It's your history book.
theysay.quick: The Bible is Israel's story opened to every nation — that's its own claim: 'a light for the Gentiles… to the ends of the earth' (Isa 49:6). If it's only one race's family record, Revelation 7:9 becomes an error.

theysay.say: You have to keep the laws, statutes and commandments to be saved. Grace is a Gentile fairy tale.
theysay.quick: Their own proof-text convicts them: 'Cursed is everyone who does not abide by ALL things written in the law' (Deut 27:26, quoted in Gal 3:10). Nobody at the podium keeps all of it. That's why Christ 'redeemed us from the curse of the law' (Gal 3:13).

theysay.say: Paul is a false apostle. He changed the Messiah's teaching for the Gentiles.
theysay.quick: Only some fringe strands say this — IUIC itself preaches from Paul. Peter calls Paul's letters Scripture (2 Pet 3:15-16), and Paul was examined by the Jerusalem apostles who gave him the right hand of fellowship (Gal 2:9).

theysay.say: The white man is Esau. Edom is the devil of this world.
theysay.quick: Edom was Israel's literal brother-nation just south of Judea — Semitic kin, absorbed into Judea a century before Christ (Herod was an Idumean). Obadiah condemns Edom for hating a brother. Reviving that hatred with the colors switched repeats Edom's sin, not Jacob's faith.

theysay.say: Where in the Bible does it say church on Sunday? Where does it say Christmas? Precept upon precept, line upon line.
theysay.quick: Notice the method: chained fragments with the chapters removed. Even 'precept upon precept' (Isa 28:9-13) is, in context, drunken scoffers mocking Isaiah — and God warning that fragment-hearing leads to falling backward. Offer to read any WHOLE chapter together.

theysay.say: That DNA test saying you're Nigerian? That's Esau's science. They control the labs.
theysay.quick: When evidence can only ever confirm the doctrine — and all contrary evidence is a plot — that's not faith, it's a closed loop. Ask gently: 'What evidence, even in principle, could show the chart is wrong?' Truth isn't afraid of testing (1 Thess 5:21).

theysay.say: The tribes fled into West Africa after 70 AD. That's who the slave traders caught.
theysay.quick: First-century Jews knew where the diaspora lived — Acts 2 lists the nations, and none of the historical record places the twelve tribes in the Bight of Benin. Genetic ancestry of African Americans traces to the exact West and Central African regions the slave-trade ledgers name.

theysay.say: Christmas, Easter, Sunday — that's Babylon. You're keeping pagan days and calling it worship.
theysay.quick: Christians have honest internal debates about holidays, and Colossians 2:16-17 gives the principle: festivals are shadows; the substance is Christ. Notice what's revealing — the camps' answer to 'Babylon' is more calendar-keeping, not the Lamb.

theysay.say: The church got you asleep, brother. Pastor's got a Bentley and you've got a burden.
theysay.quick: Some churches have failed people — concede it without flinching; Jesus reserved his hottest words for religious exploiters (Matt 23). Then ask: does a bad shepherd disprove the Shepherd? Ezekiel 34 says God's answer to false shepherds is to come shepherd his flock himself.

theysay.say: Jacob have I loved, Esau have I hated. That's talking about YOU, Edomite.
theysay.quick: If you're the white listener: stand there with grace — you're being handed a lifetime of real grievances in one sentence. Malachi 1 and Romans 9 are about God's electing purpose, not melanin. Romans 9-11 ends with 'God has consigned ALL to disobedience, that he may have mercy on ALL.'

theysay.say: We been teaching this since 1896 — before your grandaddy's grandaddy. This ain't new.
theysay.quick: True — Crowdy's church was founded in 1896, and it's worth knowing the history. But age doesn't settle truth (Mormonism is older). And the street camps' 1West doctrine only dates to 1960s Harlem — younger than most of the churches it condemns.

lessons.t: Before you engage: the megaphone is not the mission field
lessons.what: Street camps preach for the crowd, not the interlocutor. The podium, the poster, the amplifier and the circle of officers are a performance space, and 'winning' an exchange there feeds the show — clips of flustered Christians are recruitment content. The people most likely to actually hear you are the newer members at the edge of the circle, and the conversation that matters happens one-on-one, after, quietly. If the crowd is hostile or you have children with you, a warm word and a departure is not defeat.
lessons.ask: Ask yourself first: am I trying to win this crowd, or love this man? Then ask him: 'Can we talk after you're done — just us? I'll buy the coffee.'

lessons.what: It starts with an identity provocation aimed at whoever is walking past: 'So-called Black man!' — designed to stop feet and enroll the crowd. The hook is real and you should respect it: it offers a chosen people identity, an explanation for centuries of suffering, and dignity to people the world has often denied it. Don't sneer at the longing; answer the doctrine.
lessons.ask: 'What's your name, brother? I'm ___.' Names first — it converts a performance into a conversation, and it's surprisingly disarming.

lessons.what: The anchor text: verse 68's 'ships' equals the Middle Passage, so the curses prove Black Americans are Israel. It's emotionally powerful because Deuteronomy 28's horrors genuinely echo slavery's horrors. But the argument only works with the chapter closed: the ships sail to Egypt ('again'), the curse falls on the covenant nation for breaking the covenant (v.15), and the final clause — 'no man shall buy you' — inverts the Atlantic trade, where buyers were the engine of the whole evil.
lessons.ask: 'Can we read the whole chapter together — verse 15, verse 68, then chapter 30? Who is being addressed, where do the ships land, and what does God promise after the curse?'

lessons.what: Next comes the poster: twelve tribes mapped to modern peoples — African Americans as Judah, with Haitians, West Indians, Puerto Ricans, Mexicans, Native Americans and others assigned to the remaining tribes (mappings vary by camp). The chart is the movement's real creed, and its weakness is simple: no verse produces it. It is asserted, then verses are decorated around it.
lessons.ask: 'Which scripture puts each nation under its tribe? Take any single line of the chart — where does the Bible itself say that?' (There is no such verse; watch the pivot back to Deut 28.)

lessons.t: Stage four: 'Christianity was given to you by slave masters'
lessons.what: The emotional core, and the place to concede real history honestly: slaveholder religion existed, whitewashed art existed, churches were complicit. Say so plainly — flinching here costs you everything. Then the counter-history: the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8), the church in Egypt and North Africa within the first centuries, Ethiopia Christian by the 300s — 1,400 years before 1619. And the tell: the 1807 'Slave Bible' cut Exodus out, because masters knew the full Bible is an emancipation document. Enslaved believers read Exodus and knew whose side God was on.
lessons.ask: 'If Christianity is the slave master's religion, why did the slave masters have to cut the Bible apart before they'd hand it to the enslaved?'

lessons.what: The close: join the camp, keep the laws, statutes and commandments, take a Hebrew name, wake up. This is where the gospel contrast is sharpest, because their own canon supplies the verdict: Deuteronomy 27:26 curses everyone who fails to keep all of it — a standard no one at the podium meets. Galatians 3 quotes exactly that verse and answers it: Christ became a curse for us. Salvation by bloodline plus law-keeping is the one gospel Paul anathematized — and the one burden Jesus never put on anyone he called.
lessons.ask: 'On your doctrine, how many commandments can you break and still be saved? Read Deuteronomy 27:26 and Galatians 3:10-13 with me — who has ever survived that standard except One?'

proofs.they: 'The LORD shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships… and there ye shall be sold… and no man shall buy you.' Egypt means bondage generally; ships mean the Middle Passage; this is the prophecy of the trans-Atlantic slave trade, so Black Americans are the Israel of this chapter.
proofs.you: Read verses 15 and 58 first: these curses fall on the covenant nation for breaking the covenant God made at Sinai — the chapter's 'you' is the people who stood at Moab. The destination is Egypt, and 'again' points back to the exodus. And the last clause runs opposite to the Atlantic trade: 'no man shall buy you' describes a slave market with no buyers — utter worthlessness — while the Middle Passage ran on buyers. Josephus records a literal fulfillment: after Jerusalem fell in AD 70, Rome shipped captives to the Egyptian mines (Wars 6.9.2). Most of all: the chapter is not the end of the story. Deuteronomy 30 promises restoration when hearts return to the LORD — the very heart-circumcision the New Covenant delivers (Deut 30:6; Jer 31:31-34).

proofs.they: Hair like wool, feet like burnt brass 'as if they burned in a furnace' — that's an Afro and dark skin. The white Jesus is a Renaissance forgery; John saw a Black Messiah.
proofs.you: On the forgery point, agree: European portraiture made Jesus look Dutch, and that deserves the critique. But read the verse whole: the hair is 'WHITE like wool, white as snow' — wool supplies the whiteness, exactly as in Daniel 7:9 where the Ancient of Days has hair 'like pure wool.' The feet are like bronze glowing in a furnace — molten, radiant metal — and two verses on, his face is 'like the sun shining in full strength.' No complexion glows like a furnace. This is theophany-glory, and John's response settles the genre: 'I fell at his feet as though dead.' The historical Jesus was a brown-skinned Judean of Middle Eastern appearance — neither the blond of the paintings nor a proof-text for anyone's chart.

proofs.they: The Ancient of Days has hair 'like the pure wool' — the heavenly court is Black; wool hair is African hair.
proofs.you: Follow the logic where it goes: the Ancient of Days here is God the Father figure enthroned — so on this reading the text is assigning ethnicity to the eternal God, whom 'no one has ever seen' (John 1:18) and who is spirit (John 4:24). The vision's own accents are whiteness and fire: garment 'white as snow,' hair like pure wool, throne of flames. Wool in both testaments is the Bible's standard image for whiteness — 'though your sins be as scarlet… they shall be as wool' (Isa 1:18). Apocalyptic visions communicate holiness, purity and unapproachable glory, not demographics.

proofs.they: 'I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem' — the Bible's own voice declaring Israelites are Black people.
proofs.you: Read verse 6, where she explains herself: 'Look not upon me, because I am black, because the SUN hath looked upon me… they made me the keeper of the vineyards.' She is describing a field-worker's deep tan, and asking the pale city women not to look down on her for it — a class contrast inside the same people, in a love poem. If anything, the exchange assumes the daughters of Jerusalem were lighter-skinned than a sunburned vineyard girl. Ancient Israelites were Levantine people with the range of brown skin that region still has; this verse is neither embarrassed by dark skin nor a racial census.

proofs.they: 'From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering' — the scattered Israelites are in Africa, beyond Cush. That's the trans-Atlantic diaspora.
proofs.you: The verse before it gives the frame: 'then will I turn to the PEOPLES a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD' (3:9) — this is the great ingathering, worship streaming to God from the farthest horizon a Judean could name. 'Beyond the rivers of Cush' is the idiom for the ends of the earth (cf. Isa 18:1). And notice how the New Testament shows it beginning: an Ethiopian official reading Isaiah on the Gaza road, baptized by Philip (Acts 8) — Africa was in the story from the church's first decade, by grace, not by chart. The verse promises distant worshipers brought near, which is exactly what the gospel does for every nation (Eph 2:13).

proofs.they: 'To the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad' — the tribes were still scattered in bondage, and James is writing to us, the tribes lost in the Americas.
proofs.you: James wrote in the mid-first century to Jewish believers dispersed across the Greco-Roman world — a diaspora everyone could locate: Acts 2:5-11 lists its nations ('Parthians, Medes, Elamites… Egypt… Rome'), and Paul found its synagogues in every city he entered. Sixteen centuries separate this letter from 1619; you cannot re-address someone else's mail. And note the letter's first identification: James, 'a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,' writing to those who 'hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory' (2:1) — the scattered tribes he greets are defined by faith in Jesus, which is precisely the identity offered to everyone.

proofs.they: The Roman captain mistook Paul for an Egyptian — you can't mistake a white man for an Egyptian. The apostles looked African.
proofs.you: Read the next verse: the confusion ends the moment Paul speaks — 'I am a Jew from Tarsus' (21:39). The tribune wasn't studying Paul's complexion; he assumed this riot-center must be a known fugitive, the Egyptian insurrectionist Josephus also mentions. First-century Egyptians and Judeans were both eastern-Mediterranean peoples — brown-skinned neighbors, plausibly confusable, which actually agrees with the mainstream picture: Jesus and the apostles were Middle Eastern men, not northern Europeans. That's a fair correction of the paintings; it isn't a twelve-tribes chart.

didyouknow.t: The movement really does date to 1896
didyouknow.d: William Saunders Crowdy — born enslaved in Maryland in 1847, a Union Army veteran — founded the Church of God and Saints of Christ in Kansas in 1896 after visions that Black Americans descended from the twelve tribes. It's the earliest institutional Hebrew Israelite congregation, and it still exists — observing Saturday Sabbath while honoring Jesus.

didyouknow.t: There is a Hebrew Israelite village in Israel right now
didyouknow.d: Ben Ammi Ben-Israel (born Ben Carter, Chicago) led followers out in 1967 via Liberia to Israel. Today roughly 2,700-3,000 African Hebrew Israelites live mainly in Dimona — strict vegans who shun synthetic fabrics; their youth have served in the IDF since 2004. Ben Ammi received Israeli citizenship in 2013 and died in 2014.
didyouknow.src: Times of Israel; My Jewish Learning

didyouknow.t: Israel nearly deported them — then relented
didyouknow.d: In 2021 about 130 Dimona community members without status received deportation orders. After years in limbo, the community won a legal victory in May 2025 securing their ability to stay. Israeli officials attend their memorials; the mayor of Dimona has championed a neighborhood named for Ben Ammi. The state's posture is complicated — but it is not the 'impostors expelling the real Israel' story the street camps tell.
didyouknow.src: Religion News Service, May 2025; Times of Israel

didyouknow.t: '1West' is an address, not a doctrine
didyouknow.d: The militant street lineage began when Abba Bivens left Harlem's Commandment Keepers congregation in the 1960s to found the 'Israeli School' at 1 West 125th Street — hence '1West.' Nearly every shouting camp you'll meet — IUIC, ISUPK, GMS (Great Millstone), the Sicarii — descends from it by splinter after splinter, each often denouncing the others as false Israel.

Israel United in Christ — the suits-and-gold-fringes camp with the polished YouTube presence — was founded in 2003 by Bishop Nathanyel in New York. Its structure is quasi-military: bishops, deacons, captains, officers, soldiers, with the 'soldier' framing justified from 2 Timothy. The matching uniforms are deliberate street theology: impossible to ignore, and a recruitment aesthetic of discipline and dignity.
didyouknow.src: Forward; New Religious Movements; Jamaica Gleaner

didyouknow.t: The fringes are Numbers 15, and they keep a real calendar
didyouknow.d: The tassels with a blue thread on camp members' garments come straight from Numbers 15:38-39. Camps keep Sabbath from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset, and IUIC keeps Passover with lamb or goat, bitter herbs, unleavened bread and wine, plus Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Tabernacles and New Moons. Whatever else is wrong, the practice is serious — treat it with respect.

didyouknow.t: Rabbinic Judaism says no — but one Israelite rabbi built a bridge
didyouknow.d: Jewish authorities do not recognize Hebrew Israelites as Jews absent conversion. But Rabbi Capers Funnye of Chicago — raised AME, ordained in the Israelite tradition — underwent formal conversion with an Orthodox-Conservative rabbinic court, sits on the Chicago Board of Rabbis, and in 2015 became Chief Rabbi of the International Israelite Board of Rabbis. The peaceful wing of this movement talks with Judaism; the street camps shout at it.

didyouknow.t: The Nation of Yahweh is the movement's darkest chapter — and a different organization
didyouknow.d: Hulon Mitchell Jr., 'Yahweh ben Yahweh,' built a Miami empire from 1979 — and in 1992 was convicted of conspiracy in a murder campaign (14 killings, including initiation murders of white victims). He served 11 years of an 18-year sentence. Be precise here: this group is organizationally distinct from the street camps and from peaceful Israelites; use it to show where racial theology can go, never as a smear of every fringe-wearer.

didyouknow.t: The SPLC designation is camp-specific, on purpose
didyouknow.d: The SPLC lists over a hundred 'Radical Hebrew Israelite' groups as hate groups for antisemitic and anti-white teaching — and states in the same breath that most Hebrew Israelites are neither racist nor violent. The ADL draws the same line. The watchdogs distinguish street camps from the wider movement; a Christian talking to a neighbor should be at least as careful.
didyouknow.src: SPLC 'Radical Hebrew Israelites' file; ADL backgrounder

didyouknow.t: The DNA evidence points across the Atlantic, not to the Levant
didyouknow.d: A 2014-15 study in the American Journal of Human Genetics (5,269 self-identified African Americans) found ancestry averaging roughly 75% African and 24% European — with the African component tracing to West and Central Africa, the very regions the slave-trade records name. Handle with care: genetics answers the historical claim, but no chromosome makes anyone more or less an heir of Abraham (Gal 3:29).

didyouknow.t: The Khazar theory failed its genetic test
didyouknow.d: The claim that Ashkenazi Jews descend from medieval Turkic converts was tested genome-wide by more than twenty geneticists (Behar et al., Human Biology 2013): no evidence of Khazar origin; Ashkenazi Jews cluster with other Jewish communities and Middle Eastern populations. The one contrary study used modern Armenians and Georgians as stand-ins for Khazars — and was refuted on exactly that point.

didyouknow.t: Kendrick Lamar put camp doctrine on a Pulitzer-adjacent album
didyouknow.d: On DAMN. (2017), Kendrick raps 'I'm an Israelite, don't call me Black no more' ('YAH.') and closes 'FEAR.' with a voicemail from his cousin Carl Duckworth — an IUIC member — telling him Black people suffer under Deuteronomy 28's curses. Millions of listeners met 'precepts' language through those tracks. Kendrick later said he wasn't committed to the group; the doctrine still rode the album.

Kanye West defended his antisemitic outbursts by claiming 'Black people are actually Jew also,' and days later Kyrie Irving shared the film 'Hebrews to Negroes' — which calls modern Jews impostors — to millions of followers; the Nets suspended him when he wouldn't apologize. If someone in your life started using this vocabulary around then, that's likely the on-ramp.

didyouknow.t: The violent edge is real, and the movement's critics aren't inventing it
didyouknow.d: The December 2019 Jersey City kosher-market attackers, who murdered four people, had links to radical Hebrew Israelite ideology. Earlier that year, the Lincoln Memorial confrontation that went viral began with a 1West camp taunting a crowd. These are the acts of a radicalized fringe — but they're why calm, non-defensive engagement (not megaphone-vs-megaphone) matters.

week.t: Sabbath, Friday sunset to Saturday sunset
week.d: The seventh day is kept strictly — rest, assembly, teaching. Some strands (Dimona) even fast on it. It structures the entire week.
week.tip: Never schedule your coffee or invite anything for Friday night or Saturday. Honoring their Sabbath without being asked communicates respect no argument can.

week.d: Passover (with lamb or goat, bitter herbs, unleavened bread, wine), Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Tabernacles, New Moons — kept on a biblical-lunar calendar, not the church year.
week.tip: Ask what Passover was like this year, genuinely. Then, when trust exists: 'Paul calls Christ our Passover lamb (1 Cor 5:7) — can I show you why?'

week.d: Christmas, Easter, birthdays and Halloween are rejected as pagan Babylon. Expect December to be a point of friction — and of loud certainty.
week.tip: Don't die on the Christmas hill. Concede its date isn't biblical, then move to what matters: not the calendar of the celebration but the identity of the Child.

week.d: No pork or shellfish across the movement; Leviticus 11 is the baseline. The Dimona community goes further — full veganism as a return to Eden's diet.
week.tip: Eat what they eat when you share a table; Paul's flexibility (1 Cor 9:20) applies. A shared clean-food meal is worth ten street debates.

week.d: Tassels with a blue cord on the borders of clothing (Numbers 15:38), worn to be seen and asked about. Camp uniforms add insignia and titles; some strands add head coverings for women.
week.tip: Ask about the fringes — they wear them hoping someone will. It opens Numbers 15; note the tassels were to remind Israel of ALL the commandments, which leads honestly to Deut 27:26 and Gal 3.

week.d: Camps run weekly 'classes,' not services: instructor at a podium, students with notebooks, Scripture drilled by call-and-response ('Precept!'), plus scheduled street sessions that function as both evangelism and training.
week.tip: Understand that your friend isn't just attending church — he's enrolled. Counter a school with a table: unhurried whole-chapter reading, questions welcome, no podium.

week.d: IUIC runs bishops → deacons → captains → officers → soldiers; other camps use their own ranks. Advancement, uniform standards and public correction create strong belonging — and strong pressure.
week.tip: The structure meets a real hunger, especially for men: order, brotherhood, rank, purpose. Your church's answer can't be a handshake at the door. Invite him into actual responsibility-bearing brotherhood.

week.d: Strong male headship; modesty codes for women; children raised in the school. Some strands historically practiced polygamy (Dimona); street camps teach wifely submission in hard-edged terms.
week.tip: If a wife or mother in your life is navigating a husband's conversion, she needs Ephesians 5 modeled, not quoted — the head who gives himself up. That contrast preaches.

week.t: New names and a new language
week.d: Members often take Hebrew names, greet with 'Shalom,' call God 'Yahawah' and Christ 'Yahawashi' (camp-specific renderings), and prize Paleo-Hebrew lettering. Language is the badge of waking up.
week.tip: Use their name if they've changed it — it costs you nothing and removes a wall. The gospel question isn't the pronunciation of the Name but whether one has the Son (1 John 5:12).

aboutyou.t: Your faith is 'the slave master's religion'
aboutyou.d: Every conversation runs through this frame: Christianity was issued with the whip, so your gospel is the oppressor's sedative and your church a plantation artifact.
aboutyou.tip: Concede the true part fast — slaveholder religion was real, and God hates it (Rev 18:13 lists slave-trading among Babylon's cargo). Then the history: Ethiopia and Egypt were Christian over a millennium before 1619, and the 'Slave Bible' had to cut Exodus out. The enslaved met the real Bible and heard freedom.

aboutyou.d: They assume your mental Jesus is the blond of Sunday-school art, and that exposing the painting exposes the faith.
aboutyou.tip: Agree about the art without blinking: Jesus was a brown-skinned Judean, and Europeanized portraits deserve critique. Then note the Bible itself gives no physical description except Isaiah 53:2 — 'no beauty that we should desire him.' The Word became flesh to be trusted, not color-matched.

aboutyou.d: Organized Christianity — Catholic, Protestant, Black church especially — is cast as the confusion system, its pastors as hirelings keeping Israel asleep.
aboutyou.tip: Don't defend every church; defend Christ. Jesus scorched religious exploiters harder than any camp does (Matt 23), and Ezekiel 34 promises God himself will shepherd where shepherds failed. Ask: 'If some shepherds are false, who is the true one, and how would you recognize him?'

aboutyou.t: If you're white: you are Esau
aboutyou.d: In street camps you may be addressed as 'Edomite' — cursed lineage, future slave, possibly told salvation isn't available to you at all. It's designed to make you either explode or leave.
aboutyou.tip: Do neither. You're being handed centuries of real grievance in a single word — absorb it with unoffended calm (1 Pet 2:23). One honest question carries far: 'If Revelation 7:9 has every nation before the throne, who removed me?' And remember which listeners are watching how you take it.

aboutyou.t: If you're a Black Christian: you are the target audience
aboutyou.d: The camps aren't really preaching at white passersby — they're preaching at you. Expect 'asleep,' 'brainwashed,' and uglier words. Your existence as a joyful, Scripture-fluent Black Christian is the counter-argument they most need to neutralize.
aboutyou.tip: You don't have to carry the whole race-and-faith debate on a sidewalk. Your unhurried confidence — 'I know exactly whose I am' (Gal 3:26-29) — plus a standing invitation is more destabilizing to the doctrine than any rebuttal.

aboutyou.t: They expect you not to know your Bible
aboutyou.d: The method is calibrated for Christians who can't locate Deuteronomy. Rapid-fire references overwhelm; your fumbling becomes the crowd's proof that the church teaches nothing.
aboutyou.tip: Being able to open to the text, gently, changes the whole encounter. You don't need their speed — you need the contexts of five chapters: Deuteronomy 28-30, Galatians 3, Romans 9-11, Revelation 1, Acts 2. Depth beats velocity.

aboutyou.t: The precept method is the engine — and the vulnerability
aboutyou.d: 'Precepts' chain half-verses across the canon so fast that no single text is ever read whole. The chain feels overwhelming; each link is fragile.
aboutyou.tip: Never chase the chain. Pick ONE link and say: 'Let's read that entire chapter — I'll read it with you right now.' Whole-context reading is the single most disruptive thing you can do, because the method cannot survive it. (Even 'precept upon precept,' Isa 28, is scoffers being judged.)

aboutyou.t: They expect contempt or fear — warmth is the anomaly
aboutyou.d: Camp preachers are used to two responses: mockery or a wide berth. A Christian who is unafraid, unmocking, learns names, and comes back next week does not fit the script — and the script is what holds the crowd.
aboutyou.tip: Many members joined because the camp was the first place that took their questions about Black suffering seriously. Take those questions MORE seriously — the theodicy longing under the doctrine deserves a better answer than the chart, and you have one: the cross, where God entered the suffering.

aboutyou.t: Their Scripture memory is real — honor it
aboutyou.d: Whatever's wrong with the hermeneutic, many members have memorized more verses than most churchgoers, wear obedience on their clothing, and reordered their diets and weeks around the Bible. Dismissing them as ignorant is both false and fatal to the conversation.
aboutyou.tip: Say it out loud: 'You take this Book more seriously than most people I know.' Then the one question that honors and probes at once: 'So let's read it in whole chapters — if it's true, it can survive its own context.'

doctrine.theirs: The twelve tribes are today's Black Americans, Hispanics and Native Americans, each nation mapped to a tribe on the chart; 'Israelite' is a bloodline identity recovered by waking up.
doctrine.bible: Israel is the covenant people descended from Jacob — and Scripture itself says descent was never the deepest thing: 'not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel' (Rom 9:6). In Christ, everyone baptized into him is 'Abraham's seed, heirs according to promise.'

doctrine.theirs: The curses are a fingerprint identifying the true tribes: whoever suffered slavery in ships is Israel. The curses remain in force on Black people until they return to the laws.
doctrine.bible: The curses were covenant sanctions on the nation that stood at Sinai, historically executed in the Assyrian, Babylonian and Roman catastrophes. The chapter's sequel is Deut 30's promised restoration and heart-circumcision — accomplished in the New Covenant, where Christ 'became a curse for us.'

doctrine.theirs: Most 1West camps do preach Christ — as 'Yahawashi,' a Black Israelite who came only for Israel's lost sheep, i.e. the chart's nations; his death avails for Israelites who keep the law.
doctrine.bible: Jesus is Israel's Messiah for the world: sent first to Israel's lost sheep, then commissioning disciples to all nations; the Lamb purchased people 'from every tribe and language and people and nation.' A Messiah who saves one bloodline is a different Messiah.

doctrine.theirs: Nationality plus obedience: be of the tribes and keep the laws, statutes and commandments. Grace-alone is dismissed as a Gentile corruption.
doctrine.bible: 'By works of the law no flesh shall be justified' — the law's own verdict (Deut 27:26) curses every non-perfect keeper. Salvation is by grace through faith in the crucified and risen Christ, for Jew first and also Greek, producing obedience rather than being purchased by it.

doctrine.theirs: Mainstream camps use Paul heavily (IUIC preaches from his letters); some fringe strands reject him as a false apostle who invented grace for Gentiles.
doctrine.bible: Paul was confronted by the risen Christ, examined by the Jerusalem apostles who added nothing to his gospel and gave him fellowship's right hand; Peter ranks his letters with 'the other scriptures.' Reject Paul and you must also explain Luke, Acts, and Peter.

doctrine.theirs: Emphasis falls on a coming earthly reversal — Israel's national vindication, enemies subdued — more than on resurrection; teaching varies by camp and is often thin on the world to come.
doctrine.bible: The hope is bodily resurrection because Christ is bodily risen — 'the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep' — then a renewed creation where death itself is destroyed. Vindication is real, but it's Christ's, shared with all who are his.

doctrine.theirs: In extremist camps, non-tribe nations ('heathens,' Edomites) are excluded from the Kingdom or admitted only as servants of Israel; some teach whites cannot be saved at all.
doctrine.bible: The promise to Abraham was 'in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed'; Israel's calling was to be a light to the nations; the throne-room census is 'a great multitude no one could number, from every nation.' Gentiles enter as sons, not staff.

doctrine.theirs: Khazar converts and Edomite impostors occupying Israel's name and land — a counterfeit to be exposed.
doctrine.bible: Genome-wide studies find no Khazar origin; more importantly, Paul — writing about Jews who rejected Christ — still calls them 'Israelites, to whom belong the adoption… beloved for the sake of the fathers,' and warns Gentile believers against arrogance toward the natural branches. Contempt for Jews is a disqualified posture, whoever holds it.

doctrine.theirs: Esau/Edom is the white race — hairy, red, cursed to servitude; 'Jacob I loved, Esau I hated' is a racial verdict on white people.
doctrine.bible: Edom was a specific brother-nation southeast of Judea, judged for violence against Jacob (Obadiah) and later absorbed into Judea — Herod was an Idumean. Malachi/Romans 9 concern God's electing purpose in redemptive history, not melanin. 'God shows no partiality' is apostolic bedrock.

doctrine.theirs: A coming reversal: the tribes awakened, regathered and ruling, with other races destroyed or serving them — extremist camps teach Edomites become slaves, reading texts like Isaiah 14:2 as a race-swap of masters and slaves.
doctrine.bible: Isaiah 14 in context is a taunt over fallen Babylon; the prophets' finale is not slavery inverted but slavery abolished — nations streaming to Zion to learn peace, a feast for all peoples, every knee bowing to the Lamb. A heaven with slave quarters is not the Bible's heaven.

doctrine.theirs: 'Babylon' — a slave-master construct; pastors are hirelings; leaving the church is the first step of waking up.
doctrine.bible: The church is Messiah's own assembly, which he loved and bought with his blood — a body where Jew and Gentile are one new man. Corrupt shepherds are real and judged (Ezek 34), but Christ builds his church and claims it as his bride, not Babylon's.

doctrine.theirs: God is 'Yahawah' and Christ 'Yahawashi' (renderings vary by camp, derived from camp-specific Hebrew systems); using 'Jesus' or 'God' marks you as deceived.
doctrine.bible: Scripture itself moves between Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek — the apostles wrote 'Iesous' under inspiration, and 'everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved' is applied to Jesus in Greek. Salvation hangs on whose name it is, not its transliteration.

identity-claims.t: So-called Black man! You're not African, you're not 'Black' — that's a color the slave master gave you. You're a Hebrew, tribe of Judah. That's why nothing in this country works for you.

I'll tell you my name if you tell me yours — I'm ___. And listen, I'm not going to mock the question, because it's the right question: who am I, and why has my people suffered? I just want to check the answer against the whole Book.

The Book already answered. Deuteronomy 28:68 — bondage, ships. Precept: Joel 3, they sold the children of Judah. Precept: Revelation 2:9, them over in Israel are liars. It's all there if you wasn't asleep.

That's four half-verses in ten seconds, brother. Pick one — your best one — and let's read the whole chapter together right now. Deuteronomy 28: who's being addressed in verse 15? Where do the ships go in verse 68? It says Egypt, and it ends 'no man shall buy you.' Millions of our ancestors were bought. The verse describes a different tragedy.
Egypt means bondage, everybody knows that. And even if you was right about one verse, you still can't tell me who you are. DNA? That's Esau's paperwork.

Here's what I can tell you, and no one can revoke it: 'You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus… if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise' — Galatians 3. An identity older than 1619 and stronger than any chart, and it's offered to you by name, not by lineage. Come read that chapter with me after you're done here — I'm buying the coffee.

curses-reading.t: Deuteronomy 28 is our fingerprint. Slavery, ships, scattered, ruled over by strangers — you're living the curses right now. That's how you KNOW who you are.

I won't pretend the resonance isn't real — reading that chapter next to the Middle Passage is chilling, and the suffering it echoes was genuinely evil. But a fingerprint has to match everywhere, not just where it's held up. Can we read verse 15? The curses fall on the nation that received THIS covenant and broke it — the people standing at Moab.
Right — Israel broke the covenant, Israel got the curses, and the curses lasted 400 years. Acts 7:6! A nation would enslave them four hundred years. America, 1619. Do the math.

Read Acts 7:7 — the next verse. Stephen says that prophecy is about EGYPT, and it was already fulfilled at the Exodus; he's retelling Genesis 15. You can't reissue a receipt for a debt the text says was paid. And here's what the camps never read: Deuteronomy 30. After the curse, God promises to gather, restore and circumcise hearts. The chapter isn't a fingerprint kit — it's a story with an ending.
The ending is Israel keeping the laws again. That's the regathering — us, waking up, back under the commandments.

The ending is better than that. Jeremiah 31: 'I will make a NEW covenant with the house of Israel… I will write my law on their hearts… I will remember their sin no more.' And Jesus, a son of Judah, lifted the cup and said 'this cup is the new covenant in my blood.' The curse of the law landed on him — Galatians 3:13 — so it doesn't have to land on you. That's not the slave master's doctrine; that's Israel's own prophets, kept.

history-genetics.t: Them people in Tel Aviv are Khazars — converts from the Caucasus. The real Jews got shipped to the Americas. That's why they hid your history from you.

That theory's been tested, though — genome-wide, by more than twenty geneticists in 2013. Result: no Khazar signal; Ashkenazi Jews cluster with Middle Eastern populations and with other Jewish communities from Iraq to Morocco. The one study claiming otherwise used modern Armenians as stand-ins for Khazars, and got taken apart for it.
And who funded them studies? Come on. Meanwhile your 23andMe says 'Nigeria' because Esau's scientists programmed it to say Nigeria.

Brother, hear what just happened: every possible test result confirms the chart, and every contrary result is a conspiracy. That's a lock, not a key. The ancestry studies trace African American roots to Senegambia down through Angola — matching the slave ships' own ledgers, kept by men who had no reason to hide Israelites. But let me tell you what I actually think matters more.
Here it comes — 'race don't matter.' Easy to say when they didn't take YOUR name and YOUR God.

No — they took the names and gods of my ancestors too, further back; every family tree has chains in it somewhere, and yours has them close and brutal. I'm not waving that away. I'm saying the Bible itself refuses to hang salvation on ancestry: 'not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel' — Romans 9. John the Baptist told actual, verified sons of Abraham that God could raise up sons from stones. If bloodline couldn't save THEM, the chart can't save anyone. But faith in the Messiah made a eunuch from Africa an heir the same afternoon — Acts 8. That inheritance no lab and no lie can take.

law-and-salvation.t: Christ said if you love me, KEEP my commandments. Not 'believe and do nothing.' You have to keep the laws, statutes and commandments — Sabbath, feast days, dietary law. That grace stuff is how Rome put you to sleep.

I actually respect the seriousness — you've reordered your week, your plate, your clothes around this Book, and most people I know haven't reordered a lunch. So let me ask the question the Book itself asks: how much of the law? Deuteronomy 27:26 — 'Cursed be he that confirmeth not ALL the words of this law to do them.'
All of it. We keep it all. That's what the school is for — you learn precept by precept until you're walking in it.

All 613, every day, from the heart — no lust, no anger, no idol of the mind? Your own bishop can't clear that bar; neither can I. James 2:10 — stumble in one point, guilty of all. That's not me lowering the standard; that's the standard refusing to be graded on a curve. So the law's own math leaves everyone under the curse. Then Galatians 3:13: 'Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.' He kept it all, and then took the sentence.
Paul. Always Paul. Convenient how the 'curse' got cancelled right when the Gentiles wanted in.

Then leave Paul aside for a second — take Jesus at Passover: 'this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for MANY for the remission of sins.' Take David: 'Blessed is the man to whom the LORD imputes no iniquity' — Psalm 32, a man under the law throwing himself on mercy. Grace isn't a Gentile invention; it's the oldest song Israel knows. And here's the part nobody at the podium tells you: grace doesn't abolish obedience, it finally makes it possible — the new covenant writes the law on the heart instead of over your head. Come read Hebrews 8 with me and check whether that sounds like Rome or like Jeremiah.

race-doctrine.t: Esau is the white man — hairy, red, born fighting Jacob in the womb. Edomites run this world system, and Malachi said it plain: Esau have I HATED.

Let's find Edom on a map first. Esau's people settled Seir — modern southern Jordan. They were Israel's literal brothers, Semitic like Jacob's line, and by a century before Christ they'd been absorbed into Judea; Herod himself was an Idumean. History knows exactly where Edom went, and it isn't Norway.
That's the cover story. Obadiah says Esau stood by while his brother was carried off, and handed him over. Who stood on the shore while YOUR people got carried off? Who did the handing over?

And there it is — that's the real charge, and I won't dodge it: people who called themselves Christians shipped, sold and whipped image-bearers of God, and painted Jesus white while they did it. That happened. God's word for it is in the Book — Revelation 18 lists trading in 'slaves, that is, souls of men' among Babylon's damning cargo. But notice what Obadiah actually condemns Edom FOR: hating a brother. A doctrine that teaches me to hate a race back doesn't reverse Edom's sin — it re-enlists in it, jersey swapped.
Easy for you to preach 'no hate' from the winning side. God's got a day coming when the last go first — Isaiah 14, Israel's gonna rule over their oppressors, take THEM captive for a change.

Read all of Isaiah's ending, though — not just chapter 14's taunt over Babylon. Isaiah 25: a feast on the mountain 'for ALL peoples,' death swallowed up forever. Isaiah 2: nations streaming to Zion to beat swords into plows. The Bible's last picture isn't the plantation with new management — it's the auction block burned down and every nation at one table with the Lamb. I'd rather invite you to that table than win this sidewalk. And Revelation 7:9 says there's a seat there with your name on it — your real one.

movement-history.t: This truth ain't new. 1896 — Crowdy was teaching Israelite identity while your church was still segregating its own pews. We PRESERVED this. The church buried it.

You know your history, and I won't cheapen it — Crowdy founded the Church of God and Saints of Christ in 1896, born enslaved, a Union veteran, and the pew segregation he faced was a scandal against the gospel. Both things can be true: the wound was real, and the medicine still has to be tested against Scripture, not against seniority. Islam is older than 1896; Hinduism's older than both. Old isn't the same as true.
It ain't just old, it's unbroken. Crowdy to the schools to us. One line, one truth, while y'all split into thirty thousand denominations.

Gently — that's not the history. The street camps come from Abba Bivens leaving a Harlem congregation in the 1960s to start the school at 1 West 125th. And 1West didn't stay one: IUIC, ISUPK, Great Millstone, Sicarii — camps that excommunicate each other on YouTube weekly. Meanwhile Ben Ammi's people went to Dimona and live peacefully; Rabbi Funnye's congregation talks WITH the Jewish community. So when you invite me to 'Israel,' I have to ask: which one? The invitation splinters exactly like the thing it condemns.
Camps disagree on doctrine, not identity. Every camp knows WHO we are. Y'all can't even agree on baptism.

Fair hit on Christian division — it grieves God, and Jesus prayed against it in John 17. But here's the difference I'd stake everything on: Christian unity rests on a Person all the fragments confess — 'Jesus is Lord, raised from the dead.' The camps' unity rests on a chart no verse produces. When Crowdy's own 1896 church still honors Jesus, and Dimona doesn't, and 1West preaches Yahawashi for Israelites only — 'who we are' is exactly what's unresolved. 'Who HE is' is the question that settles identity. Come test that one with me — whole chapters, my kitchen table, any Sabbath evening after sundown.

practice.t: You keep Sunday, Christmas and Easter — Babylon, Babylon, Babylon. We keep the Sabbath, the feasts, the dietary laws, the fringes — like the Book says. Who's really following the Bible, me or you?

I'll give you this straight: your practice is serious, and I won't pretend Christmas's date came off Moses' desk — it didn't, and Christians honestly debate the holidays among ourselves. So I won't defend a calendar. But can I ask the question underneath the calendar? What are the feasts FOR? What was Passover pointing at, all those centuries?
Remembrance and obedience. The Most High said keep it FOREVER — Exodus 12. Forever ain't 'until Rome changes it.'

Then follow the lamb through the Book with me. Exodus 12: blood on the doorposts, death passes over. Isaiah 53: a man led 'like a lamb to the slaughter,' wounded for our transgressions. Then John the Baptist sees Jesus: 'Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.' And Paul — a Pharisee who kept more Passovers than both of us combined — writes 'Christ, our Passover, is sacrificed for us.' Colossians 2 calls the feasts 'a shadow of things to come; the substance is Christ.' A shadow is honored, not insulted, when you turn to face what casts it.
Shadows. That's how y'all delete every commandment you don't feel like keeping. Next you'll tell me the swine is clean.

No — I'll tell you what Mark 7 says Jesus taught about what defiles, and what the voice told Peter in Acts 10, and you can weigh those texts yourself; you take texts seriously, so take those. But here's my honest bottom line, brother: if you kept every feast, every fringe, every Sabbath perfectly from tonight on, Deuteronomy 27:26 would still be waiting at the end with a curse for the years you didn't. The feasts were never the door — they were the hallway. Hebrews 7 through 10 walks that whole hallway to the door himself. Read those four chapters with me — Friday night, after your sundown, your table or mine. I'll bring food you can eat.
